plan.english: Elder, the assembly sat down yesterday. The warriors want war, and the old men want peace. What do you counsel? Young one, war devours the livestock. Have you seen a burning village? I have not seen one. The enemies do steal our cattle by night. Then send a man to their chief, and ask for payment. If they do not give it, the warriors will speak. Then I will send my brother.

plan.english: Brother, the grass is gone from the field. Shall we drive the herd to the mountain? The mountain is cold, and wolves dwell there. Why do you wish this? The cows are hungry, and the young ones cry. Then let us go quickly, and I will guard them by night. Take the dogs with you! I will take them. Will you stay here with the old men? I will stay, and I will build the fence.

title: How to speak before the people

plan.english: Grandfather, teach me! How shall I speak in the assembly? Listen to the old men, and be silent. And when shall I speak? Speak when your heart is full. Say true words, and the people will hear you. And if I deceive them? Then no one will trust your word. A lie is a thief. Do you know this, child? I know it, grandfather.

plan.english: Father, your breath is weak. What shall I do for you? Son, my days are few. Hear my word, and remember it. I am listening, father. Guard the peace with the people of the river. Their grandfather and I swore an oath. And if their young men break the oath? Then go to their elders, and do not go to war. I will remember your words, father.

plan.english: By which of the two paths shall we go? The path by the river is long; the path over the mountain is dangerous. Why is it dangerous? Wolves dwell in the rocks, and last year they took two sheep. The sheep will grow tired on the long path. Tired sheep live, and the wolf does not eat them. Your word is good, brother. We will go by the path of the river.

plan.english: Husband, a stranger is standing at our door. He carries a spear. Is he an enemy? Did he speak to you? He spoke. He asked for water and milk. Whoever asks for water is a guest. Give him water, and let him sit by the hearth. And if he steals our cows by night? The dogs are watchful. Do not be afraid, wife.

plan.english: Brother, our chief is old, and he is weary. He sleeps in the assembly. He was a strong chief, and he defeated many enemies. Now the people want a new leader. Whom shall we choose? You are wise, brother, and the young men follow you. I will not speak against our chief. I will ask the elders.

title: The old men by the fire

plan.english: Grandfather, why do the old men sit by the fire through the night? They are deciding the boundary. A man speaks, and the others listen. When will they decide? When it dawns, they will decide. Lie down, child, and sleep. I will stay awake, and I will listen.

plan.english: Old men, how many cows shall we give to his kin? The payment for a man is a hundred cows. A hundred cows! Our herd is not so great. Then give seven cows and a horse. And a son of yours will shepherd their sheep for a year. And will his brothers keep the peace? They swore in the assembly. They will keep it. Then we will drive the cows in the morning.

title: The king's word to the herdsmen

plan.english: You come from the king. What is his word? The king says: drive the livestock into the fence. Why shall we drive it? The grass in the field is good. Our shepherds saw enemies at the ford. How many enemies? They are many, and they have horses with them. Then we will drive the cows in, and the boys will guard the fence. I will tell the king.

plan.english: Shall we cross the river now, or wait for the ice? The river is deep now. If we cross it, the children will die in the water. The enemies are following us. If we wait, they will seize us. Then let the warriors stand at the river, and let the women and children wait in the wagons. The frost comes quickly. Then we will wait for the ice, and the warriors will protect us.

plan.english: Wise one, my son stole a sheep. Will you speak for him in the assembly? Why did he steal it? His little sisters were hungry, and our cows died in the winter. Hunger drives men. I will speak for him, if he gives payment. He will give it; he will herd that man's sheep. Then send him to me. May the gods guard you, wise one.

We will not fight. Let us set it between the two fields. Then let the elders of both tribes stand at the stone and swear. This is good. I will say it to my king.

plan.english: Young chief, what is the strength of a people? Its warriors and its horses. Warriors die, and horses run away. Then is it its cattle? Thieves steal cattle. Then tell me, elder: what is it? The word that men keep. When a people keeps its oath, it does not fall. I will keep my word, elder.

Speak at the new assembly, and I will stand with you. You are a strong sister. Will the women stand with me? They will stand with you.

plan.english: Of-Goodly-Fame, both our herds want this pasture. Our fathers fought here. Shall we two fight, or shall we divide it? Let us divide it. You take the half by the river, and I will take the half by the mountain. And who will guard the boundary between us? Our sons. Let them swear an oath at the stone. At the full moon let us two eat a feast.
